changes: OrgMembers replaces its organization/member fetch, invite and remove networking with the existing useApiCollection lifecycle. The shared helper now accepts the resource identity field; its default remains id, while organization membership endpoints use userId for deletion and confirmed list reconciliation.

The member view remounts by account, account role, work domain, organization and organization role. It cancels obsolete reads and writes; a confirmation resolved after leaving its owning view cannot issue a deletion. A local guard prevents duplicate confirmation dialogs.

Organization discovery runs only when no connection is selected, consumes the backend id contract and remains fixed to the discovered organization for that mounted scope. Discovery failures and empty organization lists offer retry; member-list failure cannot be misreported as a confirmed empty collection.

Confirmed member mutations directly update the corresponding local row rather than triggering another full reload. Failure retains entered invitation details and confirmed rows. Shared busy state serializes actions and disables inputs; success messages survive completion. Role labels, styles and icons use one table reused by badges and invitation options.

GitHubMCPBrowser shares source metadata across tabs, placeholders, icons and link titles. It deletes the separate searched boolean, unused result timestamp and repeated endpoint/tab branches. One search result state tracks pending, success and failure.

MCP searches now use apiJson with existing credentials, backend origin and a 15 second timeout. Starting another search, changing source or leaving an account aborts the old request, whose result cannot update the new view. Errors render separately from valid empty results; malformed result fields and non-HTTP links are rejected.
Read-only MCP discovery, settings navigation, external review links, relevance/star ordering and language filtering remain available. No direct MCP execution or installation capability was added.
validationNotes: Five added UI behavior cases mount real OrgMembers, GitHubMCPBrowser, useApiCollection and the application confirmation dialog with synthetic network responses. They cover encoded organization/user identifiers, desktop/bearer credentials, duplicate writes, retained failed invitations, cross-organization receipts, malformed delete success, scoped read/write cancellation, stale confirmations, StrictMode discovery, retry and retained confirmed rows.

MCP cases cover source and query supersession, account change/logout, HTTP failure versus empty results, unsafe links, nullable descriptions/languages, filtering, ordering and absence of automatic search on opening. Existing collection consumers are included in frontendBusinessContracts.
All focused tests, lint including TypeScript, all-frontend and desktop builds, and compact-layout checks passed. Earlier prune40-70 latest baselines and final file fingerprints were verified.

The first lint pass caught unsupported exact options on testing-library role queries. Those test options were removed; role names already match exactly. The final focused run and all checks use the corrected source.
limitations: Frontend cancellation cannot undo a mutation already accepted by the server. Backend membership authorization and persistence mechanisms were not changed. Writes reconcile their confirmed receipts; concurrent edits by other clients still require the existing manual refresh.

The existing global confirmation dialog is not automatically dismissed when the member view changes, but its obsolete handler cannot issue a mutation. Successful discovery uses the current backend id response rather than the unused orgId alias fallback.

Collection identity selection is used only for the differing membership route key. Default-id consumers retain their original API contracts. Validation checks displayed membership and search fields, not every backend property.

Canceling a client search does not promise cancellation of an upstream GitHub/npm query already started by the backend. The HTTP link check is not a source trust assessment; discovery remains review-only.

No real membership or API settings were modified; no live GitHub/npm searches, production model calls, native client acceptance, full-suite run, backend rebuild, commit, push, deployment or client restart were performed. Whole-project simplification remains incomplete.
remainingCandidates: BusinessWorkbench still has independently managed read/bind/import operations and cached artifacts requiring lifecycle review.
Other organization settings and the shared confirmation dialog cancellation lifecycle have not received final project-wide acceptance in this batch.
